_meta.purpose: Context for the culture coach. These are common tendencies, not rules about any individual.
_meta.note: IN_to_JP entries use likely_read_by_japanese_partner instead of likely_read_by_indian_partner.
_meta.status: Team-authored starter set. Have a Japan-India business practitioner review before external use.

entries.likely_read_by_indian_partner: A positive signal, close to a yes: the deal is moving forward.
entries.actual_intent: Polite acknowledgement. Often a deferral and sometimes a soft no; the real answer depends on internal approval.
entries.coaching: Say what is being decided, by whom, and by when. Ask for the one thing that would help the decision.
entries.rewrite_en: We will review this internally and confirm our decision by [date]. To help us decide, could you send [document] by [date]?

entries.literal: I will handle it appropriately / do what I can.
entries.likely_read_by_indian_partner: A promise that the problem will be fixed.
entries.actual_intent: A promise of effort with no guaranteed result. Frequently used when the speaker cannot commit.
entries.coaching: Replace with a concrete action, an owner and a date, and say what happens if it cannot be done.
entries.rewrite_en: We will [specific action] by [date]. If we cannot, we will tell you by [date] and propose an alternative.

entries.likely_read_by_indian_partner: A hurdle to be negotiated; keep pushing or offer more and it may become possible.
entries.actual_intent: Usually a refusal, expressed indirectly to avoid a direct 'no'.
entries.coaching: State the decision plainly and offer what you can do instead, so the partner does not keep negotiating a closed door.
entries.rewrite_en: We are not able to accept this condition. We could consider [alternative] instead. Would that work for you?

entries.likely_read_by_indian_partner: They are weighing it and will come back with an answer soon.
entries.actual_intent: No commitment. It may mean the proposal is unlikely to proceed, or that consensus has not formed yet.
entries.coaching: Give a realistic timeline and name the next step, so silence is not misread as agreement or rejection.
entries.rewrite_en: We need time to review this internally. You can expect our reply by [date].

entries.pattern: 持ち帰って確認します
entries.literal: I will take this back and check.
entries.likely_read_by_indian_partner: A quick check; the person present will answer within a day or two.
entries.actual_intent: The attendee usually cannot decide alone. The proposal goes through internal consensus-building (nemawashi / ringi), which can take weeks.
entries.coaching: Explain the approval steps and how long they typically take, and ask who else should be briefed.
entries.rewrite_en: I need approval from [team/role]. Our process usually takes [N] days, so we will reply by [date]. Is there anyone else you would like us to brief?

entries.pattern: 少し考えさせてください
entries.literal: Please let me think about it for a little while.
entries.likely_read_by_indian_partner: A short pause before a yes.
entries.actual_intent: May be hesitation or a polite no. A real yes is usually accompanied by specific next steps.
entries.coaching: Name the concern behind the pause and set a follow-up date so the partner is not left guessing.
entries.rewrite_en: I have a concern about [issue]. Could we discuss it on [date], after we check [item]?

entries.pattern: ちょっと厳しいかもしれません
entries.literal: It might be a little tough.
entries.likely_read_by_indian_partner: Challenging but still achievable with effort.
entries.actual_intent: Typically a refusal softened by 'maybe' and 'a little'.
entries.coaching: If it is a no, say no and why. If it is conditional, name the condition.
entries.rewrite_en: We cannot meet [requirement] under the current terms. We could do it if [condition].

entries.actual_intent: Ambiguous. Can mean 'yes, that works' or 'no thank you, I don't need it'.
entries.coaching: Use an explicit yes or no, and restate what is being agreed or declined.
entries.rewrite_en: Yes, that works for us. / No, thank you, we do not need that.

entries.likely_read_by_indian_partner: Formal approval of the proposal or draft.
entries.actual_intent: No objections were raised in the meeting. It is not necessarily an approval, and concerns may surface later.
entries.coaching: Ask for written confirmation of what has been approved and list any open points.
entries.rewrite_en: We have no objections to [items] so far. Open points: [list]. We will confirm formal approval by [date].

entries.likely_read_by_indian_partner: Agreement with what was just said.
entries.actual_intent: Often only 'I am listening and following', not 'I agree'.
entries.coaching: Do not treat in-meeting nods and 'hai' as consent. Close each point with a written summary.
entries.rewrite_en: To confirm, we have agreed on [point 1] and [point 2]. Is that correct?

entries.likely_read_by_indian_partner: Full freedom to decide, with no further checks.
entries.actual_intent: Trust that the partner will act sensibly within unstated expectations. Surprises later can damage the relationship.
entries.coaching: State the limits: budget, brand rules, approvals needed and what must be reported back.
entries.rewrite_en: We trust you to handle [task]. Please keep within [limits] and let us know before [decision points].

entries.pattern: よろしくお願いします
entries.literal: Please treat this favourably / I look forward to working with you.
entries.likely_read_by_indian_partner: A courteous closing line, with no concrete request attached.
entries.actual_intent: A relationship-based expectation that the other side will follow through on what was discussed.
entries.coaching: Add the specific ask and date, so the expectation does not stay implicit.
entries.rewrite_en: Please confirm [specific item] by [date]. We look forward to working with you.

entries.pattern: Yes, no problem, it will be done.
entries.literal: Yes, no problem, it will be done.
entries.likely_read_by_japanese_partner: A firm commitment: feasibility has been checked and the deadline is safe.
entries.actual_intent: Often a sign of willingness and goodwill. Feasibility, timeline and dependencies may not have been confirmed yet.
entries.coaching: Ask for specifics: who, what, by when, and what could block it. Record the answers in the meeting minutes.
entries.rewrite_en: Thank you. Could you confirm the delivery date, the person responsible and any risks to that date?

entries.likely_read_by_japanese_partner: A sincere pledge of maximum effort that signals high commitment.
entries.actual_intent: May be a polite hedge rather than a commitment to the outcome. Check what 'best' means in dates and quantities.
entries.coaching: Translate the phrase into a measurable target and agree on a checkpoint.
entries.rewrite_en: Please tell us what you can commit to by [date], and what would need to change to reach the full target.

entries.likely_read_by_japanese_partner: A reply within hours or the same day.
entries.actual_intent: 'Shortly' is flexible and can mean a few days. It signals intent to respond, not a specific time.
entries.coaching: Ask for a date and time, and offer to schedule the follow-up yourself.
entries.rewrite_en: Thank you. Could you reply by [date, time]? If it helps, we can hold a short call at [time].
